threadListItem.$description: The sixth piece of the family — the left-rail clickable row (subject + 2-column Department/Received-style metadata + chevron + a persistent selected accent), the actual list Message Center's thread pane is built from. Built on Card's own `interactive` shell per the approved plan — hover/pressed/focused colors are the exact same semantic values Card's interactive variant already resolved to (fill.primary border on hover, bg.primary+fill.primary on pressed, border.focus ring), verified at build time against Card's real resolved values (not retyped, and not cross-referenced at the token level either — this project's components never alias a sibling component's own tokens directly, only resolve-and-compare in the build script, same discipline as every other reuse in this family). 'selected' reuses the identical pressed pair, applied persistently rather than only on click — a selected row is functionally 'as if permanently pressed'. Where the live desktop app shows an expiry as bare red-colored text ('Expires: 03/01/2027'), this component upgrades that specific value to a real Badge (danger role) instead of inventing a second ad-hoc red-text convention now that a proper component exists for exactly this. No unread indicator (dot/bold subject) — not asked for, deferred rather than built speculatively.

metadata.$description: Label:value rows, same line, spread apart (label left, value right) — matches the live app's own Department/Received/Regarding/Expires rows exactly. Both label and value at size.xs — secondary information, deliberately smaller than the subject; differentiated by color (muted vs. default), not weight.

inbox.$description: Second content shape for the same interactive row — the Message Center inbox-list layout (avatar + department identity + timestamp + subject + preview + flag + optional Expires), as opposed to the Department/Received metadata-row shape above. Avatar is a real Avatar (resolved from avatar.tokens.json, base size), keyed off the department name (not a person) — same fallback-color hashing logic, just fed a department string instead of a person's name, so 'Academic Advising' always lands on the same identity color. No 'Handled by' row and no right-aligned Expires column (both present in the live inbox screenshot) — deliberately dropped/repositioned per explicit request: Expires moves to a left-aligned row directly under the preview text instead. REDESIGNED 2026-07-24 per explicit feedback, following the staff-mockup reference: no longer a rounded, bordered card sitting in a padded/gapped list — inbox rows are FULL-BLEED flat rows (no radius, no own border, no gaps) separated by a 1px list.divider, filling the rail edge to edge. Every row is in one of two required states: 'unread' (whiter, higher contrast, heavier weights) or 'read' (grayer, lower contrast, normal weights) — see those groups below. Because a flat row has no border to color, hover/pressed leave the card shell's blue-border language and use the ghost fill.neutralHover/fill.neutralActive convention instead (list.hoverBg/list.activeBg); 'selected' keeps the persistent bg.primary fill, just without the border. The card metadata-row shape above keeps the original Card-interactive shell states unchanged.

flag.$description: 2026-07-24: the flag became a real, clickable per-thread toggle (student marks a thread important), not a static staff-side glyph. Unflagged = the OUTLINED flag icon (assets/icons/material-outlined/flag.svg — first outlined icon in the repo, sourced 2026-07-24) in icon.muted; flagged = the FILLED flag (material-filled/flag.svg) in icon.warning (yellow). Because the row now contains a nested interactive element, the inbox row is a <div role='button' tabindex='0'> with a real nested <button> for the flag — the same no-interactive-inside-interactive resolution Attachment's idle shape already established (a real <button> can't nest another one).

list.$description: The full-bleed list presentation: rows separated by a 1px divider, no per-row radius/border/gaps. Hover/pressed reuse the established ghost progression (transparent-ish rest → fill.neutralHover → fill.neutralActive) because a flat borderless row has nothing for the card shell's blue hover border to attach to.

unread.$description: A thread with activity the viewer hasn't opened yet — whiter and higher-contrast than 'read': surface.default bg, text.default identity/subject at weight.semibold, preview one step darker (text.secondary) than read's. Identity/subject keep their shared base typography (size/leading) from inbox.identity / threadListItem.subject — only weight and color swap per state.

read.$description: Already-opened thread — grayer and lower-contrast: surface.dim bg (2026-07-24: first tried surface.page — literally white, dims nothing — then surface.sunken/gray.100, which explicit feedback called too heavy next to unread's white; surface.dim/gray.50 was added to the semantic layer for exactly this), text.secondary identity/subject at weight.normal, text.muted preview.

selected.$description: The exact same pair as 'pressed', applied persistently (the row is currently open in the reading pane) rather than only for the moment of a click.
